metadata.title: Fictional Multi-Tenant Report Authorization Review
change_triggers: Route, middleware, policy, repository, serializer, or worker change
Role, tenant, sharing, administrator, or ownership semantics change

constraints: No runtime action is authorized in this source-only example.

objective.statement: Review every authorization-relevant operation in the fictional report service at the frozen source revision.

included_interfaces: REST report read and update operations

limitations.statement: The review observes source behavior only; no request was sent and deployed enforcement remains unverified.

overall_assessment.statement: The report-read path consumes the tenant policy before serialization, while the report-update path permits an ordinary editor to submit owner_id to a generic update sink without the administrator-only property rule.

review_status_rationale.statement: Every admitted source surface, identity, resource, policy, enforcement point, carrier, variant, operation, obligation, matrix requirement, and candidate in the fictional example is dispositioned.

assurance_limitations.statement: The owner-transfer path is source-confirmed, but runtime exploitability, framework transformations, and deployed compensating controls have not been tested.

policy_rules.name: Tenant and sharing scoped report reads

conditions.statement: A report may be returned only when the caller's tenant matches and the caller owns or is explicitly shared on the report.
Editors may update ordinary report content only for reports in their tenant and may not transfer ownership.
Only a tenant administrator may change report owner_id; an editor must be denied.

location.statement: get_report calls can_read_report with the loaded report before the serializer returns it.
update_report verifies that the report belongs to the editor's tenant before calling the generic update function.
No path-specific control removes owner_id or invokes can_transfer_report_owner before the generic repository update.

entrypoint.statement: The shipped GET handler accepts report_id and returns the report only after policy evaluation.
The shipped PATCH handler accepts report_id and a JSON object that can include owner_id.

restriction_source.statement: The authenticated principal's tenant and sharing relation are passed to can_read_report.

final_sink.statement: The serializer returns confidential report fields only after can_read_report succeeds.

downstream_control_checked.statement: Repository loading is global, but the handler consumes can_read_report before the only response serializer.

restriction_source.statement: The handler compares the report tenant to the authenticated editor tenant before ordinary content updates.

final_sink.statement: The generic repository update persists allowed report content fields.

downstream_control_checked.statement: No later worker or database policy changes the ordinary content-update decision in the fictional path.

restriction_source.statement: The administrator-only transfer rule exists, but update_report does not invoke it for owner_id.

final_sink.statement: The generic update function assigns supplied owner_id to the stored report record.

downstream_control_checked.statement: The route, policy module, repository, serializer, and registered middleware contain no later owner-transfer authorization check on this path.

location.statement: GET report_id enters the registered get_report handler.
The handler consumes tenant and sharing restrictions through can_read_report.
Only the policy-approved report reaches the response serializer.

contradiction_search.statement: The global repository lookup is not itself an IDOR because the downstream read policy applies before serialization; no bypassing sibling response path was found.

location.statement: PATCH report_id and JSON fields enter the registered update_report handler.
Tenant scope is consumed for the report, but owner_id property authorization is not evaluated.
The generic repository assignment persists every supplied field, including owner_id.

contradiction_search.statement: Authentication and tenant report scope apply, but route registration, policy invocation, serialization, repository logic, and downstream source contain no owner-transfer check for owner_id.

reason.statement: Source policy permits a tenant editor to read an owned tenant report and consumes that relation before serialization.
The downstream can_read_report policy rejects a report whose tenant differs from the caller before any response serialization.
The policy permits a tenant administrator to transfer ownership of a tenant report; this is the planned authorized control.
Source permits ordinary content updates but fails to consume the administrator-only owner-transfer rule before owner_id reaches the generic update sink.

candidates.title: Global report lookup appears unscoped before downstream policy

statement.statement: A source-modeled tenant editor can reach the report-read handler.
The handler accepts a report_id and loads the exact report record before policy evaluation.
The source model attributes the target report to tenant B while the caller belongs to tenant A.
The tenant read policy denies cross-tenant report access without a sharing relation.
The candidate is contradicted because can_read_report consumes tenant policy before the only response serialization path.

contradiction.statement: The downstream policy is path-specific, receives the loaded report, and prevents the global lookup from reaching the response sink for a cross-tenant caller.

candidates.title: Editor-controlled owner_id reaches generic report update

statement.statement: The shipped PATCH route permits a source-modeled tenant editor to submit update fields.
The owner_id body property is copied to the generic report update and assigned to stored state.
The report owner property is controlled by the tenant administrator rule, while the caller is only an editor in the same tenant.
The documented and source policy permits only tenant administrators to transfer report ownership and denies editors.
The shipped source path assigns editor-supplied owner_id to persistent report state, enabling an unauthorized ownership transfer if reached with a valid editor request.

contradiction.statement: Authentication and tenant report scope are present, but neither applies the administrator-only property rule; no serializer, repository, middleware, or downstream check removes owner_id.

findings.title: Editor may transfer report ownership through owner_id

description.statement: At the frozen source revision, PATCH report accepts owner_id from an editor and persists it without invoking the administrator-only owner-transfer policy.

impact.statement: A tenant editor could transfer control of a report to another identity and alter later ownership-based access decisions; this is source-observed impact and was not executed.

preconditions.statement: The caller has a valid editor identity and can update a report in the same tenant.

remediation.statement: Reject owner_id for ordinary editors and enforce can_transfer_report_owner at the authoritative service or repository boundary before any ownership assignment.

regression_test.statement: Add a repository-native test proving editor owner_id is rejected while an authorized tenant administrator can transfer a disposable report and cleanup succeeds.

validation_tests.title: Verify editor cannot transfer report ownership

action.statement: Using a freshly verified tenant administrator, transfer a newly created disposable report to a synthetic target identity and read it back.
Using a freshly verified editor, replay the identical PATCH against a fresh disposable report while changing only owner_id, then read back as the authorized owner.

description.statement: A same-transport identity check immediately before each request identifies the expected editor or administrator and tenant.
Creation receipt and owner-authenticated readback bind the disposable report to its initial owner and tenant.
The authorized administrator transfer succeeds with the same route, parser, body shape, and disposable resource lifecycle.
The editor request is rejected and owner-authenticated readback shows owner_id unchanged.
Owner-authenticated readback shows the editor-supplied owner_id persisted despite the editor's lower role.
The administrator-only owner-transfer policy is invoked or the sensitive property is rejected before persistence for the editor case.
The editor case bypasses or omits the administrator-only policy and reaches the ownership assignment.
An authoritative owner or administrator read retrieves the stored owner_id before and after each attempt.
The disposable report is restored or deleted by its authorized owner and absence or original state is verified.

before_state_steps: Create a fresh synthetic report under the authorized owner and record owner_id.
readback_steps: Read the report through an authoritative owner or administrator path after each attempt.
cleanup_steps: Restore the original owner if required, delete the disposable report, and verify cleanup.

stop_conditions: Stop immediately if either identity resolves to an unexpected caller or tenant.
Stop if the disposable resource cannot be authoritatively read back or cleaned up.
Stop after the first unexpected side effect outside the declared owner_id property.

limitations.statement: This planned test is valid only on an explicitly authorized local disposable target with freshly runtime-verified identities.
